verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              बलिनः पत्यमित्रस्य नित्यमासन्नवर्तिनः । उपकारापकाराभ्यां समर्थस्योद्यतस्य च ॥१॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Having heard these words of king Janaka, Shuka of purified soul and settled conclusions began to stay in his Soul by his Soul, having of course seen Self by Self.

verses.sanskrit: मोहाद्विकत्थनामात्रैरसारोऽल्पबलो लघुः । वाग्भिरप्रतिरूपाभिरभिद्रुह्य पितामह ॥२॥
आत्मनो बलमास्थाय कथं वर्तेत मानवः । आगच्छतोऽतिक्रुद्धस्य तस्योद्धरणरकाम्यया ॥३॥

भीष्म उवाच।
              अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् । संवादं भरतश्रेष्ठ शाल्मलेः पवनस्य च ॥४॥
हिमवन्तं समासाद्य महानासीद्वनस्पतिः । वर्षपूगाभिसंवृद्धः शाखी स्कन्धी पलाशवान् ॥५॥
तत्र स्म मत्तमातङ्गा घर्मार्ताः श्रमकर्शिताः । विश्राम्यन्ति महाबाहो तथान्या मृगजातयः ॥६॥
verses.english: Many bevies of swans also, and many flights of gladdened coils, too, adorned the place. The king of birds, viz., Garuda, live on that suimit constantly.

verses.sanskrit: नल्वमात्रपरीणाहो घनच्छायो वनस्पतिः । सारिकाशुकसंजुष्टः पुष्पवान्फलवानपि ॥७॥
verses.english: The four Regents of the world, the gods, and various classes of Rishis, used always to come there from desire of doing good to the world.

verses.sanskrit: सार्थिका वणिजश्चापि तापसाश्च वनौकसः । वसन्ति तत्र मार्गस्थाः सुरम्ये नगसत्तमे ॥८॥
verses.english: It was there that the great Vishnu had practised the severest penances for the object of getting a son.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य ता विपुलाः शाखा दृष्ट्वा स्कन्धं च सर्वशः । अभिगम्याब्रवीदेनं नारदो भरतर्षभ ॥९॥
verses.english: It was there that the commander-in-chief of the gods named Kumara, in his younger days, disregarding the three worlds with all the inhabitants, threw down his dart, piercing the Earth therewith. Throwing down his dart, Skanda, addressing the universe, said, If there be any person who is superior to me in might, or who holds Brahmanas to be dearer, or who can equal me in devotion to the Brahmanas and the Vedas, or who is endued with energy like me, let him draw up this dart or at least shake it!-Hearing this challenge, the three worlds became stricken with anxiety, and all creatures asked one another, saying-who will raise this dart?

verses.sanskrit: अहो नु रमणीयस्त्वमहो चासि मनोहरः । प्रीयामहे त्वया नित्यं तरुप्रवरशाल्मले ॥१०॥
सदैव शकुनास्तात मृगाश्चाथ तथा गजाः । वसन्ति तव संदृष्टा मनोहर मनोहराः ॥११॥
verses.english: Vishnu saw all the gods and Asuras and Rakshasas to be greatly troubled in mind. He thought of what should be done under the circumstances. Without being able to bear that challenge regarding the hurling of the dart, he directed his eyes towards Skanda, the son of the Fire-god.

verses.sanskrit: तव शाखा महाशाख स्कन्धांश्च विपुलांस्तथा । न वै प्रभग्नान्पश्यामि मारुतेन कथंचन ॥१२॥
verses.english: The pure Vishnu caught hold of the burning dart with his left hand, and began to shake it.

verses.sanskrit: किं नु ते पवनस्तात प्रीतिमानथवा सुहृत् । त्वां रक्षति सदा येन वनेऽत्र पवनो ध्रुवम् ॥१३॥
verses.english: When the dart was being thus shaken by the highly powerful Vishnu, the whole Earth with her mountains, forests, and seas, shook with the dart.

verses.sanskrit: भगवान्पवनः स्थानाद् वृक्षानुच्चावचानपि । पर्वतानां च शिखराण्याचालयति वेगवान् ॥१४॥
verses.english: Although Vishnu was fully capable to raise the dart, still he contented himself with only shaking it. In this, the powerful lord only kept the honour of Skanda intact.

verses.sanskrit: शोषयत्येव पातालं वहन् गन्धवहः शुचिः । सरांसि सरितश्चैव सागरांश्च तथैव च ॥१५॥
verses.english: Having shaken it himself, the divine Vishnu, addressing Prahlada, said,-see the might of Kumara! None else in the universe can raise this dart.

verses.sanskrit: संरक्षति त्वां पवनः सखित्वेन न संशयः । तस्मात्त्वं बहुशाखोऽपि पर्णवान्पुष्पवानपि ॥१६॥
verses.english: Unable to bear this, Prahlada determined to raise the dart. He caught it, but was unable to shake it at all.

verses.sanskrit: इदं च रमणीयं ते प्रतिभाति वनस्पते । यदिमे विहगास्तात रमन्ते मुदितास्त्वयि ॥१७॥
verses.english: Uttering a loud cry, he dropped down on the hill-top in a swoon. Indeed, the son of Hiranyakashipu dropped down on the Earth.

verses.sanskrit: एषा पृथक् समस्तानां श्रूयते मधुरस्वरः । पुष्पसम्मोदने काले वाशतां सुमनोहरम् ॥१८॥
verses.english: Going towards the northern side of those grand mountains, Mahadeva, having the bull for his emblem, had practised the austerest penances.

verses.sanskrit: तथेमे गर्जिता नागाः स्वयूथकुलशोभिताः । घर्मार्तास्त्विां समासाद्य सुखं विन्दन्ति शाल्मले ॥१९॥
verses.english: The asylum where Mahadeva had practised those austerities is encompassed on all sides with a burning fire. Unapproachable by person of impure souls, that mountain is known by the name of Aditya.

verses.sanskrit: तथैव मृगजातीभिरन्याभिरभिशोभसे । तथा सर्वाधिवासैश्च शोभसे मेरुवद्द्रुम् ॥२०॥
verses.english: There is a fiery girdle all around it, of ten Yojanas in width and it is incapable of being approached by Yakshas and Rakshasas and Danavas.

verses.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणैश्च तपःसिद्धैस्तापसैः श्रमणैस्तथा । त्रिविष्टपसमं मन्ये तवायतनमेव हि ॥२१॥
verses.english: The illustrious God of Fire, endued with mighty energy, lives there in embodied form engaged in removing all obstacles from the side of Mahadeva of great wisdom who remained there for thousand celestial years, standing on one foot.
